react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-paradigm pathway enrichment converges on Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052, SMPDB:SMP00043, MUMM:galactose_metabolism) as the dominant affected pathway across ORA (RaMP multi-DB, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) and m/z-direct (mummichog) paradigms. RaMP ORA returned this pathway ranked #1-#2 (FDR = 1.72e-12, fold enrichment = 1089.5) with 5 of 31 pathway members detected (galactitol, myo-inositol, galactinol, sucrose, glycerol); MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returned the identical KEGG:hsa00052 as top hit (p = 5.16e-08); and mummichog's m/z-direct analysis returned the equivalent MUMM:galactose_metabolism at rank 5 (p = 0.019), with a 12/13 input overlap confirming near-complete pathway coverage. Five driver metabolites are shared across all three tools: galactitol (KEGG:C01697, InChIKey first block FBPFZTCFMRRESA), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137, InChIKey first block CDAISMWEOUEBRE), galactinol (KEGG:C01235, InChIKey first block VCWMRQDBPZKXKG), sucrose (KEGG:C00089, InChIKey first block CZMRCDWAGMRECN), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116, InChIKey first block PEDCQBHIVMGVHV). The structural InChIKey first-block correspondence across RaMP (resolved to ChEBI) and mummichog (resolved to KEGG) confirms these are the same chemical entities across namespaces with no structural conflicts. A secondary convergent signal in Glycerophospholipid metabolism (WP:WP2533, REACT:R-HSA-1483206, MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism) is supported by ethanolamine, myo-inositol, and glycerol — consistent with membrane lipid remodeling downstream of galactose perturbation. Dopamine (KEGG:C03758) and 2-methoxyestradiol (KEGG:C05302) appear in androgen/estrogen biosynthesis and tyrosine metabolism pathways with weaker single-metabolite enrichment signals and do not reach consensus across ≥2 paradigms at rank ≤5. Squalene (KEGG:C00751) appears in steroid biosynthesis (hsa00100, p=0.19) but is not a driver of the primary pathway. The primary biological story is a coordinated perturbation of galactose catabolism and its downstream glycerophospholipid branch, consistent with a metabolic reprogramming phenotype in the treatment group.

RaMP ORA returned Galactosemia at rank 1 with FDR = 1.72e-12, driven by five input metabolites: galactitol (KEGG:C01697), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116). This result replicated across the KEGG namespace (KEGG:map00052 Galactose Metabolism) and mummichog m/z-direct analysis, which returned MUMM:galactose_metabolism at rank 6 with p = 0.020 and 12/13 input overlap. The convergence across ORA (RaMP), m/z-direct (mummichog), and network topology (glycerophospholipid metabolism appearing in both RaMP and mummichog results) confirms a coordinated metabolic perturbation centered on galactose handling. The five driver metabolites show consistent InChIKey first-block correspondence across namespaces, indicating they are the same chemical entities regardless of database representation. Dopamine (KEGG:C03758) and 2-methoxyestradiol (KEGG:C05302) appear in secondary hits (WP:WP3604 and WP:WP3584) but do not reach consensus at rank ≤5 across multiple paradigms.
